the influence of intracranially applied osmotically acting solutions on renal sympathetic nerve activity (RSA) in anaesthetised cats.
the influence of intracranially applied sodium chloride on renal nerve activity and renal blood flow.
the influence of intracranially applied sodium chloride solutions on renal nerve activity and blood pressure in baroreceptor-denervated cats.

the carotid body, the hypothalamus and the renal nerves are involved in the control of renal osmoregulation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the osmotic stimuli of the ICA and CVS are able to change the activity of renal sympathetic nerve endings.
osmotic stimuli of the ICA are able to induce changes in renal sympathetic nerve activity.
the carotid baroreflexes and the carotid osmoreceptors are not independent of each other but interact in a way which may influence renal function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the renal nerves are very sensitive to changes in osmotic stimuli in both the ICA and CVS, which suggests that they are a major player in the renal response to osmotic challenges.
the osmotic stimuli of the brain are able to influence the renal sympathetic activity in a way that is dependent on the osmotic stimuli and the site of application (ICA or CVS).
